node.label: Walter Benjamin
node.date_label: 1940: On the Concept of History (composition) · 1982: Das Passagen-Werk (posthumous; edited by Rolf Tiedemann) · 1999: The Arcades Project (English translation by Howard Eiland and Kevin McLaughlin)
node.description: A critic and philosopher whose reflections on historical time challenge progressive narratives and the victor’s transmission of culture. His remembrance of oppressed predecessors is a theoretical resource, while his unfinished Paris project has a separate posthumous publication history.
node.representative_figures_and_works: On the Concept of History (composition) (1940); Das Passagen-Werk (posthumous; edited by Rolf Tiedemann) (1982); The Arcades Project (English translation by Howard Eiland and Kevin McLaughlin) (1999).
node.scope_note: Selected theoretical contributions and dated texts, with original, revised, translated and posthumous forms distinguished. Source notes state actual reading extent; no complete monograph or comprehensive reception survey is claimed. Existing collective relationships and source/roster qualifications remain.

proposed_edges.relationship: Challenges homogeneous progressive time and the inheritance of culture through the victors of history.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own theses VI–IX and XIII–XIV read; this is a contribution associated with Frankfurt critical inquiry, not institutional membership or a single Frankfurt doctrine.

proposed_edges.relationship: Makes remembrance of silenced and oppressed predecessors a demand on historical representation.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own theses II–III, VI and XII read. A conceptual resource, not a title-based claim of influence on every later memory historian; separate specific reception evidence remains unchanged.

new_sources.title: German Resistance Memorial Center, biography: Walter Benjamin

verification.note: Institutional biography gives 1892–1940 and describes death during the night of 26/27 September; heading uses 27 September. Other accounts use 26 September, so this record preserves only the supported death year.

benjamin_history_primary.note: New rereading of theses I–XV, especially II–III, VI–IX and XII–XIV, in Dennis Redmond’s 2005 translation. Not a new German collation; the existing complete-theses reading and its translation qualifications remain. 1940 is composition/context, not a newly verified first-publication date.
